text:
what_serialised_means_here: ONE SUITE AT A TIME ON THE MACHINE, default threads intact -- never tests forced serial
    within a suite. The historical spurious failures (203/7 on a tree that was really 210/0) were cross-suite machine
    overload, a different problem with a different fix.
  where_single_threading_is_genuinely_required: the independent verifiers' held-out harnesses, which do mutate process-global
    env (release/verification/.../heldout-tests/mint.rs:138-141 sets XDG_STATE_HOME and HOME). That constraint must
    not migrate back to the certification suite.
  recording_requirement: every run record that reports a suite figure must also state the --test-threads value and
    the machine load. A test result without its concurrency conditions is unfalsifiable -- P2-AR-0075 omitted both
    and its 2,742 s needed a CPU-conservation argument to decode.
  planning_figure: 'MEASURED 2026-09-22 on a verified-quiet machine at default threads: 252 tests, 2,966 s wall
    (49m26s), 38,971 CPU-s, P=12.95 effective cores (65% of 20). The suite costs about 50 minutes on this tree.
    The earlier ~1,460 s (24 min) estimate was derived from a CPU calibration that the direct measurement falsified
    by ~2.4x, and is withdrawn.'
  superseded_reconciliation: 'P2-AR-0075''s 2,742 s was NOT an outlier and needed no explanation: at the measured
    W its P is about 12, indistinguishable from this run''s 12.95. The earlier ''~3 test streams / reduced --test-threads''
    account is retracted. What survives unaffected is the --test-threads=1 category error and its ~7x cost.'
  hardware: 'the guest topology is SYNTHETIC and neither published number is right. /proc/cpuinfo carries the hypervisor
    flag and shows a perfectly uniform 10 cores x 2 threads (siblings 0-1, 2-3 .. 18-19), but the real i7-12700F
    is a hybrid Alder Lake part: 8 P-cores (2 threads each) + 4 E-cores (1 thread each) = 12 PHYSICAL cores, 20
    threads. A genuine 12700F could never show uniform SMT across all cores because the E-cores have none, so WSL2
    is flattening a heterogeneous package, and the vCPU-to-host mapping is not observable from inside the guest.
